claims.text: Simultaneous wear and corrosion resistance in HEAs is governed by the in-situ formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline, passivated surface layer.
Mechanical loading dynamically forms an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
Dynamic surface grain refinement promotes formation of a dense, uniform passive oxide film.
The nanocrystalline passive layer reduces surface defect density.
An ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer can reduce friction and mechanical wear.
A compact, stable surface oxide can inhibit oxidative or corrosive attack.
Sliding in 3.5 wt% NaCl at room temperature will induce mechanical deformation sufficient to trigger dynamic surface grain refinement.
Mechanical stress produces localized plastic deformation followed by dynamic grain refinement or amorphization.
The refined surface structure enhances rapid diffusion needed for uniform passive-film formation.
Defects in the surface layer act as initiation sites for both wear and corrosion.
The dynamically nanostructured HEA will have a significantly lower wear rate than the coarse-grained matched baseline.
The dynamically nanostructured HEA will have a lower corrosion current density than the coarse-grained matched baseline.
Coupled degradation in the dynamically nanostructured HEA will be less than the sum of its separately measured wear and corrosion losses.
Pre-annealing or alloy stabilization can produce a coarse-grained control that suppresses dynamic surface refinement during sliding.
The proposed benefit requires an environment that supports passive oxide formation.
The proposed benefit requires loading sufficient to induce surface grain refinement.
The beneficial effect may be negligible in inert or non-oxidizing environments.
Similar or better wear and corrosion resistance in the coarse-grained control would falsify the proposed governing role of the dynamic nanocrystalline passive layer.

contradictions.description: The comparison is specified as using identical compositions, but alloy stabilization or alloying modifications are offered as ways to create the coarse-grained control; such modifications would generally change composition and compromise the claimed composition match.
